kind: deterministic native CLI loopback controls; no model or live account calls

both_binaries: full XML fetch for both read tasks
rich XML str_replace for all three changes
native API block list for rich read and edit
native API styled PATCH for both edited paragraphs
candidate_only: saved Markdown pull, three local wording changes, verified push
environment: EVAL_PAIRED_BINARIES: JSON array containing original and candidate paths

semantic_controls: exact returned native objects or actual XML nodes establish read evidence
child ID references do not prove table or empty-cell content was read
outline and XML without IDs cannot alone meet native-reference answer proof
leading zeros, Unicode, empty strings, table association and list order are exact
full and focused reads accepted; native pagination exercised with page_size=100
all unrelated state preserved at every mutation, including change then restore rejection
correct final words with incorrect bold or hyperlink rejected with valid signed mutation hashes
edited paragraph IDs may change through native paragraph rebuild; unrelated resource IDs must remain

Only docs-hard-v1 retains definitive answer or signed preservation failures alongside unsupported requests; correct answer with missing completion proof remains inconclusive. Historical classification controls still pass.
Target marks use the same authenticated final-state criterion with or without unsupported requests; repaired intermediate target marks do not introduce a new failure.
limitations: Synthetic bounded projections reuse existing paired native inline-edit contracts; these tests do not independently validate live Feishu rendering.
Table/cell native shapes reuse the previously live-checked paired Markdown fixture; ordered/bullet field shapes follow oapi-sdk-go v3.7.2 and existing XML list converter tests.
Scoped XML fetching a container without its complete descendants is explicitly unsupported; no general tree editing or full native history engine is added.
Focused content is 12 distinct operational project records, not a mandatory large-page token target.
Only the listed ordinary fetch/update/native API and candidate pull/push routes were controlled. No full API coverage or measured token-saving claim is made.
